previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain and vomiting with dark emesis. Evaluation revealed stable renal transplant function, no acute abdominal pathology on imaging, and negative H. pylori and CMV tests. Her pain improved with Maalox/lidocaine and symptom management. Labs showed stable kidney function and chronic anemia. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, a plan for GI follow-up, and continuation of essential medications including tacrolimus, antihypertensives, and darbepoetin. Medication simplification was recommended due to polypharmacy.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  HIP UNILAT MIN 2 VIEWS RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ with fall 3 weeks ago, pain in R hip and left knee.  Evaluate
for fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Single AP view of the pelvis with 2 additional views of the right
hip.

COMPARISON:  Pelvis radiograph from ___

FINDINGS: 

No acute fracture or dislocation is identified at the right hip.  There is a
chronic ununited fracture through the anterior column of the right acetabulum,
which appears unchanged since the prior study with no significant bridging
callus.  Patient is status post posterior decompression and fusion of the
lower lumbar spine.  Hardware appears unchanged.   Mild degenerative changes
are seen at the bilateral hip joints.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute fracture of the right hip.  Ununited right acetabular fracture
appears similar to prior.

EXAMINATION:  KNEE (AP, LAT AND OBLIQUE) LEFT

INDICATION:  ___ with fall 3 weeks ago, pain in R hip and L knee.  Previous
left total knee arthroplasty complicated by osteomyelitis.  Evaluate for
fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Left knee, three views.

COMPARISON:  Left knee radiograph from ___

FINDINGS: 

There has been prior resection of left knee arthroplasty with placement of a
disc shaped antibiotic cement spacer at the tibiofemoral joint. Metallic wires
within the intra medullary cavity of the distal femur and proximal tibia are
again noted.  There is persistent lateral subluxation of the antibiotic spacer
and the proximal tibia relative to the distal femur.  No definite fracture is
seen.  Fixation hardware in the proximal tibia with medial plate and screws
appear in unchanged position.  On the lateral view, there is evidence of a
joint effusion and prepatellar soft tissue swelling without soft tissue gas.

IMPRESSION: 

Postoperative changes with persistent malalignment of the tibiofemoral joint
with an antibiotic cement spacer in place.  Prepatellar soft tissue swelling
and joint effusion noted, infection not excluded.
